title: The Effect of an Online Self-Study Module with a Best-Practice Video on Interprofessional Patient Handoffs by Medical Students and Nursing Trainees—A Prospective, Randomized, Controlled Crossover Study
summary: When information about patients is passed on between nurses and physicians, misunderstandings can lead to treatment errors. Future physicians and nurses should therefore learn during their training how to hand over patients well. This study compares two digital learning formats: a self-study program including a video showing an exemplary handover, and an online seminar led by a teacher with accompanying reading material. Medical students and nursing trainees complete both formats in randomly assigned order. One week after each format, they take part in a practice conversation simulating a patient handover, which trained professionals rate using an assessment sheet. Participants are also asked what they learned, how satisfied they were, and how they view collaboration between the professions. The aim is to find out which learning format leads to better patient handovers.
conditions: No disease is being investigated. Medical education research in health professions training: interprofessional communication and patient handover as a contribution to patient safety.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Medical students in their third year of study at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf or nursing trainees in their first or second year of training at Düsseldorf University Hospital; written informed consent; no previous participation in a course on interprofessional patient handover.
Exclusion criteria:
Medical students outside the third year of study at HHU Düsseldorf; nursing trainees outside the first/second year of training at Düsseldorf University Hospital or a cooperating teaching hospital; missing informed consent; age under 18 years; no internet access; previous participation in courses on interprofessional patient handover.
